data.name: Birgitta
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Norse name Birgitta, meaning 'bright, strong one'. In Christian mythology, Saint Birgitta was a Swedish nun and visionary who lived in the 14th century. She is the patron saint of Europe and is known for her visions and writings.

in_greek.name: Βίργιτα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βίργιτα προέρχεται από την Σκανδιναβική γλώσσα και σημαίνει «περικεφαλαία από ευλογίες». Στους χριστιανικούς αναγνώστες, η Βίργιτα είναι μια σημαντική μορφή που αντιπροσωπεύει την ευλογία και την πνευματική ενδυσήση. Η Βίργιτα της Σουηδίας, μια σώμα χριστιανών ιερέων, ήταν μια σημαντική πηγή επιρροής για την Ευρωπαϊκή Μεταρρύθμιση και την Αναγέννηση. Το όνομα Βίργιτα έχει επίσης συνδεθεί με την πνευματική ενδυσήση και την αποστολική ζωή, καθώς και με την προστασία και την προνοια.

in_latin.name: Birgitta
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Birgitta significat «Persona divinitatis» vel «Persona divinitatis habitans». In Christianismo, Birgitta est forma importantissima, quae significat divinitatem in habitu humano. Haec forma est manifestatio divinitatis humanitatis, in qua deus habitare videtur. Birgitta sancta, virgo suecia, fuit prophetissa, mystica, et sancta, qui fuit inspirata per spiritum sanctum ad prophetiam et ad vivificandam ecclesiam. Nomen Birgitta habet etiam significatio spiritualis, in qua Christus in habitu humano habitare videtur.

in_english.name: Birgitta
in_english.meaning: Person of divine virtue, embodiment of divine love and compassion
in_english.long_meaning: The name Birgitta originates from the Old Norse word 'bergit', meaning 'person of divine virtue, embodiment of divine love and compassion'. In Christian tradition, Birgitta is a significant figure representing the divine presence in human form. The Birgitta of Sweden, a body of Christian priests, was a key influence on the Protestant Reformation and the Renaissance. The name Birgitta has also been associated with spiritual embodiment and apostolic life, as well as protection and providence. It is also a symbol of the divine love and compassion that permeates all aspects of life.

saint_reference.note: Saint Birgitta of Sweden, a Swedish saint and mystic, was a key figure in the Catholic Church and a model of Christian spirituality.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Birgitta is revered in Sweden and is considered a national heroine due to her Swedish origin and significant contributions to the country's cultural and religious history. She is also the patron saint of Europe, reflecting her influence on the broader European continent.
data.spiritual_significance: Saint Birgitta is known for her deep spirituality and visions, which have inspired countless individuals throughout history. Her writings, which include the "Revelations of St. Birgitta," are a source of spiritual guidance and reflection. Her life and teachings continue to inspire and guide those seeking a deeper connection with God.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Birgitta, a minister in Jerusalem, Israel, shares that their name Birgitta meaning "Bright, strong one" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Birgitta: Dedicated to St. Birgitta of Sweden, patroness of Europe, she embodies the spirit of compassion, purity, and prophecy. Her name inspires us to seek wisdom through prayer and to use our gifts in service to others.
